title: Affine chart calculation for an invertible tensor algebra
statement:
Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ be an affine open on which the invertible
ideal $\mathcal L$ is generated by one element $a$. Then the graded
algebra $\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal L(V)^{\otimes n}$ is generated by the
single degree-one element $a$, and its degree-zero homogeneous localization
at $a$ is canonically $A$. Consequently the standard open $D_+(a)$ is all
of $\operatorname{Proj}_A(\bigoplus_n\mathcal L(V)^{\otimes n})$, and the
resulting affine Proj is canonically $V$ over $V$.

proof.text:
Choose the basis $a$ of the rank-one $A$-module $\mathcal L(V)$. Tensoring
this basis identifies $\mathcal L(V)^{\otimes n}$ with $A\,a^{\otimes n}$,
and multiplication sends $a^{\otimes m}\otimes a^{\otimes n}$ to
$a^{\otimes(m+n)}$. Thus every homogeneous element is uniquely $r a^n$
and the algebra is the polynomial algebra $A[a]$ with $a$ in degree one.
A degree-zero fraction has the form $(r a^n)/a^n$ and is sent to $r$;
this gives mutually inverse ring maps between the homogeneous localization
and $A$. Since $a$ generates the irrelevant ideal, the standard-open cover
lemma makes $D_+(a)$ the whole Proj, proving the asserted affine
identification and its compatibility with the degree-zero structure map.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $A$ be a ring and let $I=(a)\subseteq A$ be the ideal generated by a
non-zero-divisor $a$, so that $\widetilde I$ is an invertible ideal on
$V=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$. In the Rees algebra
$\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n$, let $at$ denote $a$ placed in degree one. Then the
standard open $D_+(at)$ is all of
$\operatorname{Proj}(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n)$, and the canonical map from
$A$ to the degree-zero homogeneous localization of
$\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n$ at $at$ is bijective. Consequently the structure
morphism

$$
\operatorname{Proj}\Bigl(\bigoplus_{n\geq0}I^n\Bigr)\longrightarrow V
$$

is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
Since $I^n=(a^n)$, every homogeneous element of degree $n$ of the Rees
algebra is $r(at)^n$ for some $r\in A$. In particular every element of
the irrelevant ideal lies in the ideal generated by $at$, so the
standard-open cover lemma makes $D_+(at)$ the whole Proj.

A degree-zero fraction at $at$ has the form $r(at)^n/(at)^n$ and is the
image of $r\in A$, so the canonical map is surjective. If $r\in A$ maps to
zero, then $(at)^kr=0$ in the Rees algebra for some $k$, i.e. $a^kr=0$ in
$A$; since $a$ is a non-zero-divisor, $r=0$. Hence the canonical map is
bijective.

The structure morphism restricted to $D_+(at)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of
this bijection, hence an isomorphism, and $D_+(at)$ is the whole Proj.
